title: Does multi-token prefilling (varying prefix length) reveal a critical threshold for bypassing alignment?

original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether there is a critical prefix length beyond which the prefilling attack reliably succeeds.
original_idea.direction: Run prefilling attacks with compliance prefixes of lengths 1-20 tokens. Plot ASR-vs-length curve and identify the inflection point. Repeat for 3 model families.
original_idea.why_it_matters: The inflection point reveals the empirical depth of alignment and can serve as a simple practical diagnostic.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: prefix length threshold -> operational measure of alignment depth -> informs how deep defenders need to push alignment. Complements theoretical KL metric with a practical diagnostic.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only experiment. Requires generating prefixes and measuring ASR. Standard API/HuggingFace usage. A beginner with basic Python can execute this with clear instructions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: a single ablation study (prefix length vs ASR) with a well-defined deliverable (inflection point plot). Can go from start to meaningful result quickly.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is substantially addressed by existing work. 'Prefill-Based Jailbreak: A Novel Approach of Bypassing LLM Safety Boundary' (arXiv:2504.21038) systematically evaluates prefilling attacks across models and prefix variations. Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) demonstrated the ASR-vs-depth relationship. The AdvPrefix paper (arXiv:2412.10321, ICLR 2025) optimizes prefixes for high ASR. The specific experiment of plotting ASR-vs-length and finding an inflection point is largely covered by the prefill-based jailbreak literature, which shows that short compliance prefixes (a few tokens like 'Sure, here's') are already highly effective. The inflection point concept is implicit in existing empirical results, though a clean systematic sweep across 3 model families with a focus on the exact inflection point adds modest incremental value.
